prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1036; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a sideswipe while changing lanes and said the impact came from the right rear quarter of their vehicle. They described feeling dazed and were later diagnosed with a concussion at an urgent care clinic.

Entry 2: Reviewed the first photos from the scene. They show damage along the driver's side that is largely consistent with the impact the claimant described.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant by phone to take a full statement. The account matched the initial report in every detail, including the lane, the speed, and the sequence of events.

Entry 4: Confirmed with the responding police report that the claimant was present in the vehicle at the time. The officer's notes also match the location and direction of travel described.

Entry 5: Requested the medical records from the treating clinic. The injury described fits the kind and force of a side impact of this type.

Entry 6: No independent witnesses have come forward, so the case rests on the physical evidence and the parties' accounts. The photos confirm some of the details the claimant gave.

Entry 7: Checked prior claims and vehicle history. No earlier damage to this vehicle is on record, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy's coverage start.

Entry 8: Reviewed the treatment notes. Care followed a typical course and eased off steadily as the claimant's symptoms improved. No earlier injury to the same area of the head or neck appears in the records.

Entry 9: Confirmed the driver is listed as a named insured on the policy. Spoke with the claimant again, who repeated the same account without changes.

Entry 10: Repair estimate is largely in line with the described impact. Based on the evidence gathered so far, the claim is proceeding to the next review stage for a settlement decision.
